1 / THE QUESTIONS

How agents use world models

Before pouring water, a robot might compare two-second and ten-second predictions of its motion. Which helps it choose an action, and what should it do if the cup moves?

AWM focuses on how agents use learned world models. Topics include learning policies from simulated experience, deciding when to query a model, and responding to prediction errors.

Talks and case studies will examine the agent’s decisions alongside predictive accuracy and the cost of simulation.

1

When to imagine

How should an agent decide whether to run a simulation, extend a rollout, or gather a new observation?

  • Adaptive model queries
  • Uncertainty and useful representations
  • Value of computation and information
2

How to act

We welcome work on using predicted experience to train policies, evaluate candidate actions, and support planning.

  • Learning from imagined experience
  • Model-based planning and search
  • Video-to-action and VLA systems
3

How to recover

When predictions fail, an agent may need to observe again, replan, or update its beliefs, model, or policy. We are interested in how it chooses among these responses.

  • Failure diagnosis and monitoring
  • Re-observation and replanning
  • Model and policy adaptation

3 / THE PROGRAM

Preliminary program

We plan a four-hour session with six 20-minute invited talks, two paired case discussions, posters, and a 30-minute debate.

Debate

Should world-model rollouts be the default for long-horizon embodied tasks?

The discussion will consider latency, prediction errors, and when to take another observation.
Preliminary program, with elapsed time from the start of the workshop
ELAPSED TIMESESSION

Times are relative to the assigned workshop slot. The final date, timing, and session details will follow CVPR decisions. Each 20-minute invited-talk slot includes a 15-minute presentation and 5 minutes of Q&A.

Paired research cases

The first session compares agent strategies using the same world model; the second examines responses to prediction failures. Each session includes two six-minute presentations and eight minutes of discussion.

The AWM card

Speakers will be asked to end with a slide summarizing the task, agent decision, result, resource budget, and a limitation. We plan to publish these slides as a casebook with their permission.
